title.narrative: Assam Integrated Flood and Riverbank Erosion Risk Management Investment Program - Project 2

description.narrative: Incorporating lessons from Project 1, Project 2 for $60.16 million will fund a combination of structural and nonstructural measures in the three subproject areas (Palasbari-Gumi, Kaziranga, and Dibrugarh) along the Brahmaputra River in Assam. The structural measures will include: (i) 20 kilometers (km) of riverbank protection works with innovative technologies, combined with 5 km of pro-siltation measures; (ii) upgrade of 13 km of flood embankments; and (iii) construction of four sluice gates and one pumping station to improve drainage. Monitoring and adaptive maintenance of the infrastructure will also be included to cope with the highly dynamic morphological processes of the river. The nonstructural measures will continue the methodologies used under Project 1 and cover community involvement and community-based flood risk management activities.

title.narrative: Loan 3755: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 25 Nov 2024
Progress Toward Outcome: Project physically closed on 18 October 2020. Actual achievement to be measured during the project completion report.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Dec 2021: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/38412/38412-033-apfs-en_0.pdf
Some results are in the Initial Environmental Examination | Jun 2020: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/38412/38412-033-iee-en_4.pdf
Some results are in the Resettlement Plans | Aug 2018: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/38412/38412-033-rp-en_5.pdf
Some results are in the Social Monitoring Reports | May 2021: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/38412/38412-033-smr-en_1.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: CBFRML consulting firm engaged to complete the activities including establish disaster management committees (DMCs).
All originally envisaged major civil works have been awarded and substantially completed.
Flood and erosion management plan with gender-inclusive elements has been updated.
Financial Management Manual has been prepared and approved by FREMAA. The Project implementation plan, financial management plan, flood forecasting, and early warning system is under implementation. The first trial run of the Flood forecasting model was carried out during the monsoon of 2019 and was continued in 2020.
GIS-based erosion prediction envisaged for the pilot stretch using imageries, and other statistical data on the structural performance for the embankment breach assessment.
Training to WRD officials has been undertaken.
